name: Unsane
label: AmRep
lede: Chris Spencer, Pete Shore and Charlie Ondras put a decapitated subway corpse on the first Unsane cover, lost their drummer to an overdose, and then got a skateboard-wipeout video that cost a couple hundred dollars onto MTV.

eras.title: Scum rock in the East Village
eras.text: Spencer, Shore and Ondras start a band at Sarah Lawrence and end up in an Alphabet City where heroin sells in the lobby. The first album disappears along with its label boss, and the second goes out with a corpse on the sleeve.

years.h: Three Sarah Lawrence students start a band called Lawn-Chair-Blisters
years.p: [[Chris Spencer|9a653ece-8339-4e2e-b893-106b13c4dbc3]] plays guitar and sings, Pete Shore plays bass, [[Charlie Ondras|0405bd1e-7edd-41b9-bc0b-ca8ef8f464ba]] drums. The name doesn't last, and they rename the band Unsane.
years.xp:
The trio moves into the East Village. Spencer told Louder he shared an apartment at 8th and D with Ondras, in a building where dealers sold heroin in the lobby from 2 a.m. to 10 a.m.

Their first show, per the same interview, was at a Lower East Side club with the Reverb Motherfuckers, in front of roughly 20 people. The practice space they shared with the Honeymoon Killers and Pussy Galore.

years.h: Improvised Munitions disappears with its label boss
years.p: Unsane record it with Wharton Tiers for Circuit Records. The owner hands Spencer a test pressing at the Pyramid Club, then is gone.
years.xp:
The owner was a man named Ernie. Spencer told Bandcamp Daily: "He completely vanished off the face of the earth." He had heard about Ernie's cocaine habit and that he probably owed a lot of money to dealers.

The album stayed unreleased for over 30 years. Louder says a copy eventually turned up in a used record store three blocks from Spencer's apartment, and Unsane's own label put it out in 2021.

years.big: "It didn't seem like 'making it' was an option."
q: We were scum rock from the drug-addled, violent, Lower East Side of Manhattan.
yt: Live at CBGB Record Canteen, February 1989
years.h: Cop Shoot Cop moves into the practice space
years.p: The room sits four or five blocks from CBGB, ABC No Rio and the Pyramid Club. Spencer is close with Sean McDonell of Surgery.
years.xp:
Helmet's Page Hamilton, Spencer told Louder, said early on that his band would "play like three shows, as big as possible, and then hit up a label for a lot of money." That wasn't Unsane's plan.

Ondras also drummed on two [[Boss Hog|57648c1f-335d-4216-ba82-508b23b3bcf4]] records, Drinkin', Lechin' & Lyin' (1989) and Cold Hands (1990).

yt: El Mundo, live at CBGB, January 1990
years.h: A 2 a.m. CBGB set after Sonic Youth gets them a deal
years.p: Gerard Cosloy, co-founder of Matador Records, approaches the band afterward and offers to sign them.

years.cap: Cover of Unsane's 1991 debut on Matador
years.h: The debut ships with a decapitated body on the cover
years.p: Unsane, cut in January at Fun City Studios, comes out on Matador with a corpse on subway tracks across the front.
years.xp:
Louder says the photo came from a friend of Shore's who worked as a police photographer; Wikipedia says the image came from someone who worked on the actual investigation. Spencer said it "kinda spoke to the harsh nature of the record."

AllMusic's Patrick Kennedy, per Wikipedia, called it a brilliant and daring debut that mixed the harshness of [[Swans|3285dc48-9505-469d-ad8a-bdf2d3dba632]] and [[Foetus|934c6bbc-3fc4-4d4a-9280-f02856da0e12]] with punk and classic-rock hooks. Spencer told Vice that real blood in art was taboo in the AIDS era.

eras.title: Ondras dies, Atlantic arrives
eras.text: Ondras dies in June 1992 and Vinnie Signorelli takes over the kit. Total Destruction comes out on Matador and Atlantic in 1994, the year Shore leaves.

years.h: Matador gathers the 7-inches on Singles 89–92
years.p: Thirteen tracks, including Burn, Urge to Kill and Blood Boy.

years.h: Charlie Ondras dies at 25 during the New Music Seminar
years.p: A heroin overdose in New York, according to Wikipedia. The band had been touring the debut.
years.xp:
Spencer told Louder that Ondras was an "occasional user, not a junkie" and that he himself was a daily user. Asked if the death was a wake-up call, he said: "Not really, not immediately."

Later he decided he didn't want to be a junkie lifer on the Lower East Side. "So I chose to get in the van and get away from it."

yt: Live at Lounge Ax, Chicago, November 6, 1992
years.h: Foetus and Swans drummer Vinnie Signorelli takes the kit
years.p: Anthony DeLuca sits in briefly first, then [[Vinnie Signorelli|8e1d0d17-1272-4418-ace5-3d6f3bde0daf]] replaces Ondras for good.

years.h: Unsane keep Total Destruction cheap to owe Atlantic less
years.p: Tracked at BC Studio in Brooklyn with Martin Bisi for $25,000, it comes out January 18 on Matador and Atlantic.
years.xp:
Spencer told Louder the band was "pretty bummed and pissed, because we never wanted to be on a major label." Atlantic still paid for a video for Body Bomb, in which Cop Shoot Cop's Jack Natz straps on a bomb and blows up the World Trade Center.

MTV's reply, as Spencer remembers it: "Don't like the band. Don't like the video." Wikipedia adds that Vox later put the cover on its list of the fifty worst sleeves.

years.h: Pete Shore leaves, and Dave Curran picks up the bass
years.p: Wikipedia gives no reason for Shore's exit. [[Dave Curran|7ce793e3-5530-4e32-a3f8-1b6661fe3205]]'s first record with the band is Scattered, Smothered & Covered.

eras.title: Minneapolis, a skate video, a Vienna hospital
eras.text: Unsane hole up in the AmRep basement to make Scattered, Smothered & Covered, land an MTV hit nobody planned, move to Relapse, and finish the decade with Spencer in surgery.

years.h: A Minneapolis winter in the AmRep basement
years.p: Unsane record for Amphetamine Reptile Records from January to May with engineer Tim Mac.
years.xp:
Spencer told Vice the band holed up for a few weeks between tours in the AmRep offices, where label boss [[Tom Hazelmyer|d6569a63-5da9-41fa-a5c9-b6b11b496218]] ran a studio in the basement.

Decibel put the record in its Hall of Fame in 2012. The title nods to a Waffle House order.

years.h: Skaters wipe out, and MTV plays it anyway
years.p: The Scrape video has skaters bailing and only six seconds of the band, and it gets heavy rotation.
years.xp:
Spencer told Louder the idea came during a bong session, while he was living at the back of an art gallery on Ludlow Street that showed skateboard art: "Could we make a skate video where everybody gets hurt?"

Louder puts the cost at $169; Wikipedia's band page says $200. The album's other clip was for Alleged.

yt: Scrape, live in New York, September 9, 1996
years.h: The lineup stops changing
years.p: Curran on bass and Signorelli on drums stay behind Spencer for more than twenty years, apart from the early-2000s break.

years.h: Occupational Hazard moves the band to Relapse
years.p: Relapse Records releases the fourth album, recorded at Excello Studios in Brooklyn with Billy Anderson and Bruce Hathaway and mixed by Dave Sardy.
years.xp:
Spencer told PopMatters the songs got "tour tight" from playing them live before release. Per Wikipedia, part of the record was cut analog and remixed at a midtown studio by Sardy.

AllMusic's Blake Butler compared the album to getting hit by a semi.

years.big: "A couple of weeks later, I was on tour for ten months, wearing a girdle."
q: They thought I was military because I was wearing camo pants.
years.h: Camo pants get Spencer attacked in Vienna
years.p: Four people attack him after a 1998 show, and he needs major surgery for internal bleeding.
years.xp:
PopMatters reports exploratory surgery, part of the small intestine removed, and staples to close the wounds. Spencer said that in hindsight the band should have rested before the ten-month tour, not after it.

Wikipedia says the injury and heavy touring led to a long break.

eras.title: A tattoo shop and a long quiet
eras.text: Spencer moves to California, Signorelli opens a tattoo shop in Queens, and Curran keeps playing.

years.h: Cutthroats 9 and a tattoo shop fill the quiet
years.p: Spencer and Curran make an album as The Cutthroats 9 for Man's Ruin, while Signorelli opens a shop in Middle Village, Queens.

eras.title: Back, and no quieter
eras.text: Unsane regroup in 2003 and keep going until 2019, with albums on Relapse, Ipecac, Alternative Tentacles and Southern Lord.

years.cap: Chris Spencer, Dave Curran and Vinnie Signorelli, 2005
years.h: Seven years on from Occupational Hazard, Blood Run
years.p: Relapse releases the first Unsane studio album since the break.

years.h: Ipecac releases Visqueen, produced by Andrew Schneider
years.p: Pitchfork's Marc Masters hears the sound intact but slicker.

years.cap: Chris Spencer and Dave Curran on stage in Hamburg, July 2011
years.h: The Melvins take Unsane on the road behind Wreck
years.p: Alternative Tentacles releases it, cut at Translator Audio in Brooklyn with Andrew Schneider. The tour runs April and May.

years.h: Between Unsane records, Spencer starts UXO
years.p: Steve Austin of [[Today Is the Day|c5790c27-5808-42a2-b409-5395b56c209f]] joins him, and a self-titled album follows in 2016 on Reptilian Records.

years.h: Unsane write Sterilize in three cities
years.p: Southern Lord releases it September 29, with songs traded between band members as audio files.
years.xp:
Curran told Vice: "We wrote songs separately and sent each other audio files, added parts, tweaked others." The ten tracks were cut down from more than 90 minutes of material.

Spencer on the New York he grew up in: "It's been sterilized from what I grew up in."

years.h: Spencer leaves Unsane and starts Human Impact
years.p: He announces it in August, with Phil Puleo, Chris Pravdica and Jim Coleman in the new band.

eras.title: Starting over, in order
eras.text: Spencer revives Unsane in 2021 with a new rhythm section and a label that reissues the old catalog chronologically.

years.h: Eric Cooper and Jon Syverson join, and Unsane come back
years.p: Spencer reforms the band with bassist Cooper and drummer Syverson, focused on early material.
years.xp: Louder says an Early Cuts European tour started May 4, 2023, at the Bastard Club in Osnabruck, Germany, with DesertFest London on May 6.

years.h: The new label starts with the lost 1989 album
years.p: Improvised Munitions & Demo is the first release on Lamb Unlimited: seven original songs plus four demos.
years.xp:
Spencer runs the label with longtime manager Todd Cote. He told Bandcamp Daily: "We're going to do it from the beginning, chronologically, one by one."

He described the old production as having "values that call to mind a rat-infested sewer."
